definitions.explanation: A frog — a small jumping amphibian that lives in or near water. Usually written in katakana as カエル, though the kanji {蛙|かえる} also exists.

examples.english: There is a frog in the pond.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{田|た}んぼ→田んぼ：00402_tanbo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧カエル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捕|つか}まえた→捕まえる：01214_tsukamaeru⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often caught frogs in the rice paddies.

notes:
Frogs are a familiar part of the rural Japanese landscape, especially in and around rice paddies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カエル⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧: frogs croak
- {雨蛙|あまがえる}: tree frog (lit. rain frog)
- カエル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捕|つか}まえる→捕まえる：01214_tsukamaeru⟧: to catch a frog

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{井|い}の{中|なか}の{蛙|かわず}→井の中の蛙：06144_inonakanokawazu⟧: a frog in a well — someone with a narrow view of the world (uses the older reading かわず)
